title: Push a camlock tension rod out to both shelf walls at an angle, twist to lock its length, and swing it level to wedge
instruction: Set the tension rod at an angle between the shelf's side walls, twist its tubes to lock the length, then swing it level so it wedges.
context: Setting a tension rod as a guard bar across a shelf is a common household act: RV ownership is at a record high, with 11.2 million US households owning an RV in 2021 (RV Industry Association), and RV guides advise a short tension rod across the front of each open shelf so items do not fall during travel, and the 2025 Go RVing owner profile reports about nine RV trips a year, so owners set and reset these rods before each trip; the same rod guards home pantry and cupboard shelves. A twist-lock (camlock) rod is set by extending it against both walls at an angle, twisting its two tubes to lock the length, and swinging it level so it wedges. If the length is locked short the rod drops at the first bump and the cans fall; if it is too long it will not swing level. The twist is a torque couple on two coaxial tubes 15.9 mm and about 13 mm across, so one hand must hold the outer tube still while the other turns the inner, and the locked length must be within a few millimetres of the 80 cm gap.
setup: A cupboard bay on the table, bench-built from 3/4 in birch plywood panels (Home Depot 206120918) with screws and glue: 18 mm board shelf with side walls 80 cm apart (inner faces), a back panel and three sealed 15 oz cans (Del Monte Golden Sweet Whole Kernel Corn, 15.25 oz) at the back. A Kenney Twist & Fit camlock tension rod, 28-48 in, 5/8 in, white (KN633NP), lies on the shelf near the front, set to 75 cm tip to tip (tape) and unlocked, its right end cap by the right wall.
scoring: Cumulative, judged at the end. 0.33: rod off the shelf with both end-cap faces against the side walls (real trial: ruler). 0.67: also cam locked (inner tube turned to the cam's lock angle, 80 deg in sim, measured on the real rod by protractor, 60-120; the rod then holds its length when pulled by hand). 1.0: also the rod held hands-off for 5 s (whole gripper over 30 mm away), level within 3 deg of horizontal (inclinometer on the rod, vertical angle only; a skew in depth is not counted), 12 +/- 1.5 cm above the shelf (ruler), then a 10 N push down at mid-span sags it under 5 mm (push-pull gauge, ruler). Void (0): the rod rests on the shelf or the cans.
fidelity: Rod at maker sizes (15.9 mm outer tube, 245 g, 71-122 cm). Estimates, each with a real-trial measurement and range in the README: inner tube 13 mm (12.7-14.3); cam holds 150 N (80-200) once turned 80 deg (60-120), 0.15 N m to turn (0.1-0.2); caps give up to 4 mm at 25 N/mm (20-40); friction 1.0 (0.5-1.0). Walls rigid; grip 40 N.
scores: Scripted demo 1.0 (step 1016, 50.8 s) and 1.0 at five corners of the estimate ranges; unlocked push-and-level 0.0; squeezed level unlocked 0.0; never letting go 0.67; level but skewed in depth (commanded 4.0 deg, measured 4.3) 1.0; off level (commanded 4.5 deg, measured 5.1) 0.67. Dream-1 policy: 0.
reset_notes: Nothing random: the rod starts collapsed and unlocked on the shelf at the same pose each run.
